data.name: Ismailat
data.long_meaning: Mother of Ishmael (Ismail) in Islamic tradition. She is the wife of Prophet Abraham (Ibrahim) and the mother of Ishmael and Isaac. Her name is derived from the Arabic word ‘ism’ meaning name and ‘ila’ meaning God.
data.spiritual_meaning: Ismailat signifies the embodiment of devotion and submission to God. Her name is a reminder of the sacrifice and obedience of Prophet Abraham, who was ready to offer his only son as a sacrifice to God.
data.numerology_meaning: Indicates new beginnings, leadership, and independence.

in_arabic.name: إسميلات
in_arabic.meaning: اسم مشتق من اسماعيل، عليه السلام، ويعني الله يسمع
in_arabic.long_meaning: اسم إسميلات هو اسم علم مؤنث، مشتق من اسم الإمام اسماعيل عليه السلام، ويعني الله يسمع، ويستخدم في بعض الثقافات الإسلامية كاسم للبنات، ويرتبط بالإيمان والتوكل على الله

in_urdu.name: اسميلات
in_urdu.meaning: اللہ کے سنتے ہوئے، اسماعیل کا مشتق، سلامتی اور برکت
in_urdu.long_meaning: اسميلات ایک علم اسم ہے، جو حضرت اسماعیل علیہ السلام کے نام سے مشتق ہے، اور اس کا مطلب ہے اللہ کے سنتے ہوئے، یہ نام بعض اسلامی ثقافتوں میں بنات کے لیے استعمال کیا جاتا ہے، اور یہ إيمان، توکل اور برکت کا प्रतीک ہے

data.cultural_impact: The story of Ismail and Hagar is a significant one in Islamic culture. It speaks of Hagar's unwavering faith and commitment to her son, and her interaction with Allah (God) during her trials as a mother, such as being left in the desert with her son, faithfully submitting to the Will of Allah. This story is celebrated with various traditions and rituals, including the annual Hajj pilgrimage.
data.spiritual_significance: Hagar, known as Ismailat in Islamic tradition, represents steadfastness, submission, and trust in Allah. Her story is a reminder that even during testing times, Allah provides sustenance and sustains His creatures. It teaches the importance of patience, trust, and obedience in the face of hardship and trials. Overall, her story is a reflection of the human condition and the journey towards closeness to Allah.
